# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
FIVE, and the first three are mine.

1. A FINDING FILED FROM A SUMMARY NAMED THE WRONG FILE. M2 said deliver
   certifies a project that did nothing. Reproducing it first showed deliver
   was correct and the hole was one file upstream, in task creation. The fix
   is smaller because of the reproduction and would have been in the wrong
   place without it. REPRODUCE BEFORE FIXING, even when a trusted reviewer
   names the file.

2. A CLAIM WAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE WRONG COPY. I proved the chain reaches
   every session by running the session-start script IN THE REPOSITORY. Real
   sessions read the installed clone, which does not have it. Verified, and
   about the wrong thing. VERIFY ACROSS THE INSTALL BOUNDARY.

3. A GATE WAS RUN OVER A MOVING TREE. The first full run reported
   test_bm_hookbench FAIL. The same suite passed 53 tests on a clean tree
   minutes later. The tree had changed underneath the measurement, twice, from
   a concurrent session. Cost: one 22-minute run. Caught only because the tool
   refuses to report green on a dirty tree.

4. TWO CLAIMS I DELIVERED WERE REFUTED BY AN ADVERSARIAL PASS. "Shipping needs
   no push" was false: the published tag carries the version string and neither
   of the two files it is supposed to carry. And the escalation tool had two
   real defects found by executing attacks, not by reading: a passing attempt
   cleared an unresolved forcing condition, and punctuation manufactured
   distinct approaches into a false escalation.

5. A WRITER LANE DUPLICATED WORK ANOTHER SESSION HAD ALREADY LANDED, for
   twenty minutes, because nothing checks whether the work already exists
   before a lane is dispatched and the fence system cannot see across repos.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
